result_summary: The prospective Stage-1 Temporal-Order promotion replication supported the bounded six-neuron two-channel temporal-order claim on 20 fresh predeclared paired seeds. The frozen decoder classifies three presented states: forward, reverse, and simultaneous. The reported forward/reverse intact accuracy median of 1.0 and identity-destroyed accuracy median of 0.0 refer to correct classification of the presented forward/reverse conditions; the simultaneous-control value of 1.0 is a separate simultaneous-class task-adequacy accuracy, not forward/reverse order accuracy. The paired forward/reverse delta median was 1.0 with bootstrap CI [1.0, 1.0], and the exact paired sign-test p-value was 1.9073486328125e-6. The human review explicitly records perfect-score saturation as a methodological limitation and does not extend the result to memory, cognition or general temporal reasoning.

human_review.decision_scope: supports CLAIM-S1-TEMP-001 only within the frozen six-neuron, two-channel task

review_basis.human_review: The reviewer assessed the reported preregistered results and explicitly conditioned supports on clarification of the simultaneous-control semantics, documentation of perfect-score saturation, and preservation of the narrow claim boundary.
review_basis.repository_verification: The frozen preregistration, runner, statistics and raw evaluation data were subsequently checked against the stated conditions. This repository verification is not represented as additional human inspection.

simultaneous_control_clarification.decoder_rule: simultaneous if first output_A spike and first output_B spike occur on the same tick
simultaneous_control_clarification.observed_behavior: In intact simultaneous trials, both first output spikes occur on the same tick and decoded_order is simultaneous; therefore success_fraction=1.0 means correct detection of simultaneity, not 100% forward/reverse order accuracy.
simultaneous_control_clarification.interpretation: The value 1.0 is not a chance-level order-decoding result and does not by itself indicate a non-temporal shortcut. It verifies that the frozen decoder distinguishes the simultaneous case as designed.
simultaneous_control_clarification.residual_methodological_question: Because all intact forward/reverse trials and all simultaneous controls are perfectly classified across the registered seeds, the task may be too easy to discriminate temporal coding from simpler deterministic path-following or decoder shortcuts under harder perturbations.

perfect_score_limitation.observation: Intact forward/reverse accuracy=1.0, identity-destroyed accuracy=0.0, paired delta=1.0 and bootstrap CI=[1.0,1.0] across all 20 seeds.
perfect_score_limitation.consequence: The result establishes the bounded task behavior but does not quantify robustness margin, mechanism uniqueness, generalization, or difficulty scaling. Ceiling/floor saturation reduces mechanistic resolution.

human_review.allowed_interpretation: Within the registered six-neuron acyclic two-channel Small-SNN task and frozen decoder, preserving logical A/B channel identity supports correct decoding of the fixed forward/reverse temporal order, while the matched identity-destroyed arm removes that order signal. The simultaneous control behaves as preregistered by producing equal first-output ticks and the decoder label simultaneous.
prohibited_interpretations: robustness to harder perturbations not tested here
limitations: The task is intentionally very small: six neurons, four synapses and two logical channels.
Perfect ceiling/floor separation across all seeds may reflect a task that is too easy to resolve robustness margin or exclude all shortcut strategies.
The simultaneous control is a preregistered task-adequacy control, not an inferential order-accuracy endpoint.
The identity-destroyed arm collapses both logical events onto physical input_A; it proves dependence on channel identity under this task but does not identify a unique neural mechanism.
This is an internal promotion replication and not independent scientific replication.

follow_up_required.purpose: stress-test decoder/task internal validity without modifying the present evidence
suggested_tests: jitter the forward/reverse gap while freezing decoder rules prospectively
swap physical channel labels after network construction to test label shortcuts
introduce balanced amplitude/current perturbations that are independent of logical order
add near-simultaneous nonzero gaps to measure temporal resolution instead of only perfect separation
use a held-out decoder or blinded decoder mapping where feasible
follow_up_required.evidence_role: exploratory planning only; not required to reinterpret or invalidate the current bounded claim unless a prospective follow-up contradicts it

human_review.comments: Supports the narrowly scoped claim under the frozen preregistered protocol. The simultaneous-control value of 1.0 is clarified as correct simultaneous-class detection, not order accuracy. Perfect-score saturation remains a material limitation and motivates a separate prospective decoder/task stress test. No learning, memory, cognition, scaling, biological-equivalence or general temporal-reasoning claim is supported.

decoder_class_semantics.forward_reverse_accuracy: accuracy for correctly classifying the presented forward/reverse condition
decoder_class_semantics.simultaneous_accuracy: separate accuracy for correctly classifying the presented simultaneous condition; not forward/reverse order accuracy

limitations: Internal promotion replication only. Scope is limited to the registered six-neuron, four-synapse, two-channel acyclic Small-SNN task and the frozen decoder. Perfect ceiling/floor separation limits mechanistic resolution and motivates a separate prospective stress test. No learning, memory, order memory, cognition, general temporal reasoning, biological equivalence, scaling, 5D superiority or independent external replication is established.
